_comment: Part 7.2 competitor capture. Comparison and alternatives pages render from this
file so a price change is one edit, not twenty.
captureMethod records how each entry was obtained. 'primary-source' means the
vendor's own pricing page was read on capturedOn. 'pending' means the page is
fully client-rendered and returned no prices to the build environment — those
entries carry NO invented figures and must not be published until captured.

competitors.name: systeme.io

affiliateProgram.note: Highest headline rate of any adjacent program. Verify terms before promoting.

competitors.pricingModel: Per contact, tiered. Unlimited email sends on every plan, 0% transaction fees.

tiers.name: Unlimited
tiers.includes: Unlimited contacts, sub-accounts, free migration service

competitors.vsGoHighLevel: Dramatically cheaper and genuinely has a free tier. Has sub-accounts at $97. Not an agency platform though — no white-label client sub-account model at GHL's depth, no native phone system, no SMS.
competitors.bestFor: Solo operators and small course businesses who want funnels, email and courses in one place at a tenth of the price.
competitors.weakness: No native telephony or SMS. Not built for managing many client accounts.

competitors.name: Keap
competitors.pricingModel: Per contact, tiered, with metered messaging on top

usage.note: Usage over the plan allotment. Keap's SMS is roughly 2x GoHighLevel's $0.00747 per segment before carrier fees.

competitors.vsGoHighLevel: Starts at $299 against GoHighLevel's $97, and that is for ONE business. No agency sub-account model, no white-label, no rebilling. Per-contact pricing scales against you.
competitors.bestFor: A single established service business that wants CRM and automation with a gentler learning curve.
competitors.weakness: Expensive per contact, no agency architecture, messaging costs roughly double GoHighLevel's.

competitors.name: Kajabi
competitors.pricingModel: Flat tiers by contacts, websites and admin seats. No revenue sharing.
competitors.vsGoHighLevel: Different job. Kajabi is a course/membership business platform; GoHighLevel is agency infrastructure. Kajabi's courses and communities are more mature; it has no phone system, no sub-account reselling, no white-label agency model.
competitors.bestFor: Creators selling courses and memberships who want polish over breadth.
competitors.weakness: No telephony, no agency model, and materially more expensive than GoHighLevel at the top tier.

competitors.name: Vendasta
competitors.pricingModel: Unusual: $0 subscription with a monthly WHOLESALE SPEND MINIMUM. Each $1 spent on select products offsets $1 of the platform fee.

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.note: At signing, the $99 platform fee covers month one.

competitors.vsGoHighLevel: The closest structural competitor for agencies reselling software. But the commercial model is opposite: GoHighLevel charges a flat fee and lets you resell its own tooling; Vendasta charges nothing up front and requires a wholesale spend commitment, with a 1-year contract above Starter.
competitors.bestFor: Agencies reselling a marketplace of third-party products rather than one platform.
competitors.weakness: Annual contracts above the entry tier, and a spend minimum that is a floor rather than a ceiling.

competitors.name: Housecall Pro
competitors.pricingModel: Per user tiers, billed annually or monthly

tiers.name: Essentials
tiers.includes: Routes — group and sequence jobs to cut drive time

competitors.vsGoHighLevel: NOT a substitute — they do different jobs. Housecall Pro runs the work: scheduling, dispatch, routing, invoicing, job costing. GoHighLevel runs the lead: capture, follow-up, nurture, reviews, booking. Many contractors end up paying for both, which is the honest answer nobody selling either one gives.
competitors.bestFor: Home service businesses that need to schedule, dispatch and invoice jobs in the field.
competitors.weakness: Marketing automation and lead nurture are thin next to a dedicated CRM. Per-user pricing bites as crews grow — $100/mo per extra user above five.

priceComparisonNotes: GoHighLevel Starter at $97 undercuts Keap's $299 entry by a wide margin, and Keap's entry is for one business with no agency model.
systeme.io at $97 for its top tier is the genuine budget alternative, but it has no telephony and no agency sub-account architecture.
Keap charges $0.015 per SMS against GoHighLevel's $0.00747 base — roughly double, though GoHighLevel's carrier surcharges narrow that gap to around 40%.
Kajabi Pro at $499/mo costs more than GoHighLevel Agency Pro at $497 and does a much narrower job.
Vendasta is the only captured competitor with an agency reselling model comparable to GoHighLevel's, and it charges through a wholesale spend minimum rather than a subscription.

Housecall Pro ($59-149/mo) and GoHighLevel ($97/mo) are complements, not alternatives. HCP manages jobs; GHL manages leads. A contractor running both is paying roughly $156-246/mo before usage — worth stating plainly rather than pretending either replaces the other.
